title: Could I Leave My Bag Here?
prerequisites: Knows common place and time words.
observable_outcome: Ask permission to leave an item somewhere until a stated time, then acknowledge the answer.
learning_objective: Use Could I + base verb + object + place + until + time? to ask permission in a travel situation.

scenario.prompt: Checkout is at 11:00. Your train leaves at 15:30. You want the hotel to keep your bag.
scenario.model: Could I leave my bag here until three?

language.grammar: Could + subject + base verb forms a permission question. No do/does is added.
language.meaning: Could I...? asks permission. Here, leave means put an item somewhere where it stays.
language.appropriateness: Could I...? is a polite permission request. Can I...? is also common. May I...? is more formal.
language.time_phrase: Until three means the bag may stay there up to three o’clock.

options.text: Could I leave my bag here until three?
options.feedback: Yes. Could I asks permission. Leave stays in the base form.

options.text: Could I left my bag here until three?
options.feedback: After could, use the base verb: leave, not left.

options.text: Could you leave my bag here until three?
options.feedback: This asks the other person to do something. The target asks permission for your action.

activities.prompt: What does until three mean here?

options.text: The bag can stay there up to 3:00.
options.feedback: Yes. Until marks the end point of the time period.

options.text: The bag must arrive at exactly 3:00.
options.feedback: No. Until describes how long the bag may stay.
No. The request is for storage after checkout.

activities.prompt: Reception says: Yes, you can leave it behind reception. What response fits?

options.text: Thanks. I'll collect it at three.
options.feedback: Yes. It acknowledges permission and confirms the collection time.

options.text: Thanks. I collected it at three.
options.feedback: That sounds like a past event. The collection is still in the future.

options.text: Could I leave your bag here?
options.feedback: That changes the object. You are talking about your own bag.

transfer.situation: After a meeting, you need to leave a parcel at reception until 4:00.
acceptable_responses: Could I leave this parcel here until four?
Can I leave this parcel here until four?
Is it okay if I leave this parcel here until four?
rubric: The action and object are clear.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, complete: Could I leave ___ here until ___?

visual.alt_text: A four-part sentence map shows permission, action and object, place, and time limit: Could I | leave my bag | here | until three?
visual.text_equivalent: PERMISSION: Could I | ACTION + OBJECT: leave my bag | PLACE: here | TIME LIMIT: until three
